notes.meaning: An earthly high priest had to be a human being so he could truly represent other people before God. His main duty was to present gifts and sacrifices to cover sins, which are our wrongdoings against God. This reminds us that sinful people cannot approach God on their own without a mediator to bring them together.

Because the human priest was imperfect and weak, he could understand the failures of others and treat them with patience. He was called to show gentle mercy to those who stumbled through ignorance or weakness rather than judge them harshly. Knowing his own frailties helped him care deeply for fellow sinners.

Because the priest shared the same sinful human weakness as the people, he had to offer sacrifices for his own sins first. Only after cleansing his own guilt could he present offerings on behalf of the nation. This showed that the earthly priesthood had limits, pointing to the need for a sinless savior.

No man had the right to appoint himself as high priest or claim that honor by his own choice. A person had to be chosen and called directly by God, just as Aaron was in the Old Testament. Serving God as a leader requires God's own calling rather than personal ambition.

In the same way, Jesus did not promote Himself or claim the role of high priest on His own authority. God the Father gave Him that honor, announcing that Jesus is His unique royal Son. Christ's priesthood rests entirely on the Father's appointment and eternal love.

God also promised that the Messiah would be a priest forever, following the pattern of Melchizedek from the book of Genesis. Melchizedek was both a king and a priest whose office never ended, unlike Aaron's family line where priests died and were replaced. This means Jesus serves as our priest without interruption and for all time.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics see Melchizedek bringing bread and wine to Abraham as a preview of Christ offering His body and blood under the forms of bread and wine in the Mass.

notes.meaning: During His earthly life, Jesus experienced deep human sorrow and prayed with loud cries and tears to the Father, who could rescue Him from death. He submitted completely to God's will in the garden of Gethsemane and on the cross. God answered His prayer by giving Him strength to endure His suffering and by raising Him from the dead.

Even though Jesus was God's beloved Son, He was not shielded from suffering. He was never rebellious, but through painful hardship He learned by personal experience what it truly costs to obey. His life shows us that God uses difficult times to teach us humble obedience to His will.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teach that learning through suffering is only God's second best and that believers should only learn through His word, though commentators reject this since Jesus Himself learned through suffering.

notes.meaning: By completing His path of suffering and giving His life, Jesus was fully prepared and consecrated as our complete Savior. He became the eternal source of salvation, delivering all who believe and obey Him from the power of sin. Our everlasting rescue depends entirely on what Christ accomplished for us.

After finishing His earthly work, Jesus was openly addressed and greeted by God as the eternal High Priest like Melchizedek. This confirmed that His priesthood is royal, complete, and superior to the old temple order. Believers can take comfort knowing their Priest continually represents them in heaven.

The author had many deep things to teach about Melchizedek and Christ, but could not easily explain them because the listeners had grown sluggish. The issue was not that the truth was hidden, but that their hearts had become lazy and inattentive. When Christians stop paying close attention to God's word, they lose their ability to take in deeper truths.

These believers had followed the faith long enough that they should have been ready to teach others about Christ. Instead, they had drifted backward and needed someone to reteach them the very first ABCs of God's word. They had become like babies who can only drink milk instead of growing people who eat solid food.

Anyone who can only take in milk is still a spiritual baby, lacking experience in the deeper message of God's righteousness. Such believers have not yet developed the spiritual maturity needed to understand full Christian truth. God loves His young children, but He does not want them to remain infants forever.

differ.view: Methodists understand milk to include foundational doctrines like justification by faith, teaching that believers should not remain content there but press onward toward holiness.
Baptists understand the message of righteousness as the gospel of Christ's imputed righteousness, which spiritual infants are still learning to understand and rely upon.

notes.meaning: Solid spiritual food is meant for grown Christians who have practiced their faith over time. By regularly using God's word, they have trained their spiritual senses to tell the difference between good and evil. This steady habit helps them spot false teachings and make wise, godly choices in daily life.

differ.view: Methodists understand maturity here as reaching a state of Christian perfection where the heart is fully governed by love.
Baptists see this maturity as growth in spiritual knowledge and discernment, holding that no believer attains complete perfection in holiness in this earthly life.
